recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-34400 unless the Security WG separately chooses broader editorial polishing of the security narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-34400 was a Published FHIR-core Security WG change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking the security page to mention OWASP prominently and add language directing implementers to OWASP API, general Top Ten, and mobile Top Ten vulnerability guidance.
initial_application: Commit 563e56f35b35b9f94193094afca019ec08e2b63c changed source/secpriv-module.html by replacing the older mobile-specific OWASP link with an OWASP root link and adding the requested OWASP vulnerability paragraph. Follow-up commits b4e095e9d5221a68a52e95ec700470e45e0a654b and 491030063623e64881b2578641b6a95575ce57ad adjusted the paragraph while preserving the requested guidance.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml includes source/secpriv-module.html as the active Security and Privacy module page. Security WG minutes from 2021-12-06 record the FHIR-34400 OWASP wording discussion and 8-0-0 vote. The Zulip Security Jira Tasks thread confirms the intent was to make implementers who find the FHIR security page take security seriously and reference OWASP. FHIR-34404 and FHIR-25939 were applied in the same historical commit but concern separate security guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/secpriv-module.html already links to OWASP near the start of the Security section and immediately follows with the OWASP API, Top Ten, and mobile Top Ten paragraph. The remaining minor typography in the existing sentence does not change the requested implementer-facing guidance and was left for ordinary editorial cleanup rather than issue-reconcile source work.
